title: Speaking Part 1: Kebiasaan dan Preferensi
topic: Membicarakan kebiasaan dan pilihan pribadi dengan frekuensi yang tepat
objectives: Menyebut seberapa sering sesuatu dilakukan dengan kata keterangan yang tepat

vocab.exampleId: Saya lebih suka teh daripada kopi.

vocab.example: Normally, the shop opens at eight.
I read in my spare time.

block1.tip: Untuk frekuensi, gunakan always, usually, often, sometimes, dan never. Kata seperti frequently dan occasionally lebih formal, sehingga cocok untuk Speaking yang lebih panjang.

youtube.videoDescription: Video 10 sampai 15 menit tentang cara membicarakan kebiasaan dan preferensi, dengan contoh kata keterangan frekuensi.

lesson.intro: Pertanyaan tentang kebiasaan dan preferensi sering muncul di Speaking. Gunakan kata keterangan frekuensi untuk menunjukkan seberapa sering sesuatu dilakukan, lalu jelaskan alasan pilihanmu.

sections.heading: Seberapa sering
sections.bodyMd: **Usually** dan **normally** menunjukkan kebiasaan umum. **Regularly** dan **frequently** menunjukkan sesuatu yang sering dilakukan. **Occasionally** menunjukkan sesuatu yang hanya kadang-kadang.

sections.heading: Preferensi
sections.bodyMd: Gunakan **prefer** dengan pola prefer X to Y. Kata benda **preference** dipakai untuk menyebut pilihan secara umum. Kamu juga bisa menyebut **enjoy** untuk kegiatan yang disukai.

sections.heading: Kebiasaan dan waktu luang
sections.bodyMd: Sebut **habit** kalau kebiasaan itu penting bagimu. Untuk menjelaskan kegiatan di waktu luang, gunakan **spare time**.

block3.title: Cara Warga Menghabiskan Waktu Luang
block3.text:
Many people think they know how they spend their spare time, but a closer look often reveals surprising habits. A recent community survey asked residents about their leisure activities, and the answers showed clear patterns. Most people said they enjoy quiet activities at home, although their preferences changed with age.

Younger residents said they frequently meet friends in cafés and parks. They usually go out on weekends, and many of them prefer activities that involve music or sport. Their habit of checking phones during meals was also common, although most admitted it was a bad habit. Some said they occasionally put the phone away for an evening, but this was not a regular practice.

Older residents had a different preference. Many of them normally read newspapers in the morning and take a walk in the early evening. They said they enjoy gardening, and a large share of them spend several hours on it each week. Their habits are more regular, and they often plan their days in advance. Some also exercise regularly at the local sports centre.

Working parents reported a different pattern. Because their time is limited, they rarely have a full evening free. They try to do one shared activity each week, such as cooking or a short trip, and they say this habit has become important to the family. Several parents described a preference for simple plans that do not need much money.

The survey also asked about the reasons behind these choices. Cost was mentioned by about a third of respondents, while lack of time was the most common reason. Distance from parks or sports centres was another factor, especially for people who live far from the centre of the city. Many people also said that their habit of staying home was partly a result of tiredness after work.

The researchers concluded that leisure is shaped more by daily routine than by personal interests alone. Those who have a regular schedule are more likely to enjoy outdoor activities, while those with unpredictable work often rely on short, easy pastimes. The city council plans to use these findings when it designs new parks and community programmes.

For anyone who wants to change their habits, the study offers a simple lesson. Start with a small, regular activity that fits your current routine, and gradually increase the time you spend on it. Small changes tend to last longer than large promises.
